# US-China competition in near-term advanced atmospheric propulsion: hypersonics, detonation engines, combined cycle

Researched 2026-10-06. Status labels used throughout:
- **[V]** verified: the source page was fetched this session and states the fact.
- **[S]** from search-result summaries only (page not fetched in full). Treat as reported, not checked.
- **[U]** a claim from Chinese state media, a Chinese journal or company PR, relayed by SCMP or others, with no independent confirmation.
- **[M]** recalled from model memory, not checked this session.

Caveat: the newest edition of CRS R45811 I could read is **27 Aug 2025** (congress.gov returned 403; I used the everycrsreport mirror). FY2027 figures come from the CRS LRHW In Focus (Apr 2026) and from reporting on the July 2026 GAO report.

## China: programs, test milestones, detonation and scramjet claims, and which claims are unverified

### Takeaway
China has fielded several operational boost-glide and hypersonic anti-ship systems: DF-17, DF-27 (now assessed by DoD as fielded, including an anti-ship variant) and YJ-21. It also tested an orbital glide vehicle in 2021 and has the world's most capable hypersonic ground-test facilities (JF-12, JF-22). Its "exotic" engine claims (Mach 16 detonation engines, kerosene oblique detonation, RDE drones) come almost entirely from Chinese journal papers reported by SCMP. They are short-duration ground tests or design studies, not demonstrated flight systems.

### Cited Findings
**Fielded or tested weapons**
- DF-ZF HGV fielded around 2020 (range about 1,200 miles). DF-17, its MRBM carrier, is "now fielded" (about 1,000-1,500 miles). [V] — [CRS R45811, 27 Aug 2025](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)
- The DoD 2025 China Military Power Report (released Dec 2025) is the first to treat the DF-27 as a fielded system: a conventionally armed ICBM-range missile (5,000-8,000 km) with an operational ASBM variant. That range covers Hawaii, Alaska and parts of CONUS. The 2024 report had said the DF-27 may carry HGV, conventional land-attack, anti-ship and nuclear payloads. [S]/[V partial] — [Andrew Erickson summary of 2025 CMPR](https://www.andrewerickson.com/2025/12/key-pentagon-china-military-power-report-reveal-df-27-conventional-icbm-has-asbm-variant-can-range-part-of-conus/); [USNI News](https://news.usni.org/?p=119931). The fetched Erickson page confirmed the DF-27 range and dual role but not the "fielded" wording; that wording comes from search summaries.
- The quote "China has the world's leading hypersonic missile arsenal" is attributed to the 2025 CMPR in secondary coverage [S] — [Eurasian Times](https://www.eurasiantimes.com/china-deploys-df-27-worlds-1st-conventional-icbm-that-threatens-to-cripple-u-s-navy-hit-hawaii-alaska-pentagon-report/). Earlier US intelligence officials used similar wording [S] — [NTSA/National Defense, Jul 2024](https://www.ntsa.org/news-and-archives/2024/7/24/testing-top-of-mind-as-us-lags-china-in-hypersonics-race). I could not confirm the exact wording in the CMPR text.
- YJ-21 (Eagle Strike-21) is a ship-launched hypersonic anti-ship ballistic missile. It was shown launching from a Type 055 in 2022 and has been in service since 2022. Estimated range is 1,000-1,500 km, average speed about Mach 6, terminal speed about Mach 10. An air-launched YJ-21E was photographed on a J-10C in Dec 2025. [S], sourced to Wikipedia, so performance figures are estimates — [Wikipedia YJ-21](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YJ-21); [Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/?p=32654)

**2021 orbital glide (FOBS-like) test**
- July 27, 2021: China launched a fractional-orbital system carrying a hypersonic glide vehicle around the Earth. A second test was reportedly held Aug 13. Gen. Milley called it "very close" to a Sputnik moment. Air Force Secretary Kendall described an orbital approach as "a way to avoid defenses and missile warning systems." Beijing said it was a reusable "space vehicle" test. [S] — [Al Jazeera, 27 Oct 2021](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/27/us-general-china-missile-test-very-close-to-sputnik-moment); [CBC](https://www.cbc.ca/lite/story/1.6227301). CRS dates it to "August 2021" [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html). The dates conflict: the FT reported July 27 and Aug 13, and CRS says August.

**Ground-test infrastructure**
- CRS lists JF-12 (Mach 5-9), JF-22 (Mach 30, completed 2023), and FD-02, FD-03 and FD-07 (Mach 8, 10 and 12). [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)
- TWZ reports that the JF-22 Mach 30 tunnel was used to test a spaceplane mothership design [S] — [The War Zone](https://twz.com/chinas-new-mach-30-wind-tunnel-tests-space-plane-mothership-design)

**Engine claims (all [U]: Chinese journal or press via SCMP)**
- Kerosene (RP-3) oblique detonation engine: CAS Institute of Mechanics researchers reported sustained oblique detonation waves in tests in the JF-12 shock tunnel. They claimed an operating envelope of Mach 6-16 and combustion "1,000 times faster" than scramjets. The tested condition was about Mach 9, with run times limited to about **50 ms** by the tunnel. Published in the Journal of Experiments in Fluid Mechanics (Nov 2024), reported Feb 2025. [U] — [Interesting Engineering, citing SCMP](https://interestingengineering.com/innovation/china-worlds-first-kerosene-powered-engine); [China Daily e-paper, 28 Feb 2025](https://epaper.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202502/28/WS67c0f318a310f4a5fb061dd3.html)
- "Mach 16" air-breathing RDE (the "most powerful detonation engine"): a Beijing Power Machinery Institute team led by Zhang Yining published a design in the Journal of Propulsion Technology. They claim it could in theory take off from a runway, climb above 30 km and reach Mach 16. This is a design and concept paper. [U] — [SCMP](https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3246361/revolutionary-design-chinese-scientists-invent-most-powerful-detonation-engine-hypersonic-flight)
- FB-1 RDE drone: Chongqing University's institute and Thrust-to-Weight Ratio Engine (TWR, Shenzhen) reported a maiden flight in Gansu. SCMP itself noted that images show the engine running during taxi and that it is "unclear whether the engine continued to operate during the flight." [U] — [SCMP](https://amp.scmp.com/news/china/science/article/3235502/explosive-engine-test-drone-could-propel-china-supersonic-age)
- A 600-second RDE run was claimed in May 2025. [U], seen only as a search-result headline — [Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/science/story/racing-ahead-of-us-china-claims-600-second-rde-test-in-hypersonic-push-raising-global-military-stakes-477808-2025-05-26)

**Test cadence**
- Former USD(R&E) Michael Griffin said China had "conducted 20 times as many hypersonic tests as the United States." [V], as quoted in CRS — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)
- Gen. VanHerck (NORTHCOM) said China's hypersonics effort is "tenfold" what the US has done. [S] — [Air & Space Forces](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/vanherck-chinas-efforts-of-hypersonics-tenfold-what-us-has-done/)
- An industry CEO claimed the US ran about 9 tests in about 5 years, against "hundreds" for China. [S], anecdotal — [NTSA, Jul 2024](https://www.ntsa.org/news-and-archives/2024/7/24/testing-top-of-mind-as-us-lags-china-in-hypersonics-race)

### Inferences
- What China has fielded is boost-glide technology on mature solid rockets (DF-17, DF-27, YJ-21). That is the near-term military reality. Its detonation and scramjet engine claims are research-stage. Run times of milliseconds in shock tunnels are far from a flightweight engine.
- SCMP's "Chinese scientists say" pieces are the main channel for the most sensational claims. They should be treated as signals of research direction, not capability.

### Gaps
- I did not find a public, authoritative count of Chinese hypersonic flight tests per year. The "20x" and "hundreds" figures are officials' statements, not data.
- I did not verify the Sept 2025 Beijing parade hypersonic displays (reported YJ-17, YJ-19 and others) [M].
- I could not fetch the 2025 CMPR PDF itself.

## US: programs, failures, fielding status and budgets as of 2026

### Takeaway
The US fielded its first hypersonic weapon in 2025-26: the Army LRHW/Dark Eagle, with a battery at JBLM receiving operational missiles in spring 2026. This came after a run of 2021-2023 test failures. Navy CPS ship tests have slipped to FY2027. ARRW was revived into procurement after its development was "completed" in 2024. HACM is behind schedule. Spending runs to billions per year, but is small next to AI and other modernization lines. The US is behind China in fielded quantity and in test cadence, though it was roughly 5-8 years behind in first fielding rather than in basic know-how (my inference).

### Cited Findings
**LRHW / Dark Eagle (Army, common hypersonic glide body)**
- Failures: Oct 21, 2021 booster failure ("no test"); June 2022 full missile test failure; Mar 5, 2023 countdown halted; Sep 6, 2023 cancelled during pre-flight checks. [V] — [CRS IF11991, 29 Apr 2026](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-04-29_IF11991_937112f05e67689e7630942387d534ce39c8625b.html)
- Successes: June 28, 2024 end-to-end flight from Hawaii, more than 2,000 miles to the Marshall Islands; Dec 12, 2024 from Cape Canaveral (first live fire with the operational battery operations center and launcher); Mar 26, 2026 launch from Cape Canaveral. [V] — same source
- Fielding: Bravo Battery, 1-17 FA (3rd MDTF), was activated at JBLM in Dec 2025. On Mar 20, 2026 the Army said that battery would "receive its first operational missiles soon." A battery has 1 operations center, 4 launchers and up to 8 rounds. [V] — [CRS IF11991](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-04-29_IF11991_937112f05e67689e7630942387d534ce39c8625b.html); [Defense Magazine](https://www.defensemagazine.com/article/us-army-activates-first-dark-eagle-unit-hypersonic-milestone-bolsters-indo-pacific-deterrence) [S]
- Cost: CBO (Jan 2023) estimated about $41M per missile, and the Army said the FY2025 fly-away cost exceeds that. FY2027 request: $446.6M RDT&E and $301.8M procurement. [V] — [CRS IF11991](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-04-29_IF11991_937112f05e67689e7630942387d534ce39c8625b.html)
- GAO (July 2026): Lockheed produces "six to seven of the 12 rounds needed per year," citing labor-intensive builds and quality problems. The Army plans to buy 48 missiles. [V] — [Stars and Stripes, 20 Jul 2026](https://www.stripes.com/branches/navy/2026-07-20/hypersonic-missile-navy-army-delay-2027-22317106.html)

**CPS (Navy)**
- Successful tests in June 2024, Dec 2024 and April 2025. [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)
- GAO (July 17, 2026): the first ship-based flight test slipped to Q3 FY2027 (it was planned for 2025), and Zumwalt integration is about 24 months behind. Program cost rose from about $31B (2020) to about $41B (2024). Missile buy was cut from 262 to 224 at about $67M each. Navy and Army combined plan more than $50B. [V] — [Stars and Stripes](https://www.stripes.com/branches/navy/2026-07-20/hypersonic-missile-navy-army-delay-2027-22317106.html); [Army Recognition](https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2026/u-s-navy-delays-zumwalt-hypersonic-missile-test-to-2027-as-costs-reach-2-billion) [S]
- FY2027 CPS request is $1.8B, up 135% from $763M in FY2026. It includes the first procurement of 12 missiles and 59 across the FYDP through FY2031. Zumwalt was 94% through modification in Jan 2026, and the three-ship conversion now costs at least $2B. [S] — [Army Recognition](https://www.armyrecognition.com/news/navy-news/2026/u-s-navy-delays-zumwalt-hypersonic-missile-test-to-2027-as-costs-reach-2-billion); [Janes](https://www.janes.com/defence-intelligence-insights/defence-news/industry/pentagon-budget-2027-us-navy-bolsters-munitions-funding)

**ARRW, HACM, HAWC, DARPA**
- ARRW (AGM-183A, Lockheed): final development test in March 2024, after earlier failures [M: 2021 failures]. FY2026 request is $387.1M procurement, moving it into production. [V]/[S] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html); [DefenseScoop, 26 Jun 2025](https://defensescoop.com/2025/06/26/air-force-arrw-procurement-funding-fy26-budget-request/)
- HACM (Raytheon/Northrop scramjet cruise missile, built on HAWC): FY2026 request $802.8M, with development through FY2029 [V] — [CRS](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html). GAO found the first design review six months late (Sep 2024), cutting planned flight tests from 7 to 5. First flight testing is targeted in FY2026. [S] — [DefenseScoop, 11 Jun 2025](https://defensescoop.com/2025/06/11/gao-report-air-force-hacm-hypersonic-cruise-missile-behind-schedule/). I found no confirmation that HACM has flown as of Oct 2026.
- DARPA HAWC (scramjet) flew successfully in 2022-2023. The HAWC, OpFires and MoHAWC programs have concluded. [V] — [CRS](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)

**Budget totals**
- FY2025 request: offensive hypersonics $6.9B, plus $182.3M MDA hypersonic defense. FY2026 request: $3.9B offensive, plus $200.6M defense. FY2026 line items: CPS $798.3M; LRHW $513M RDT&E and $354M procurement; HACM $802.8M; ARRW $387.1M. [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html). The FY2026 drop may partly reflect funding moved into the reconciliation bill or programs ending [inference, not verified].
- Test infrastructure: DoD spent about $1B on hypersonic facility modernization in FY2015-24. Test spending in FY2021-25 was about $1.09B for boost-glide and about $221M for cruise missiles. A 2014 inventory counted 10 DoD ground-test facilities, 11 open-air ranges, 11 mobile assets, 9 NASA, 2 DOE and 5 industry/academic facilities. [V] — [CRS](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)

**Commercial and industry detonation and combined-cycle work**
- Venus Aerospace flew the first US flight test of a rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE) in May 2025 at Spaceport America. It burned for 7 s at about 2,000 lbf thrust, reaching about 4,400 ft and about 383 mph (subsonic). Venus plans to pair the RDRE with its VDR2 ramjet for runway-to-Mach 4-6 flight. [S], company-sourced — [Military & Aerospace Electronics](https://www.militaryaerospace.com/commercial-aerospace/article/55290679/venus-aerospace-conducts-first-us-flight-test-of-rotating-detonation-rocket-engine)
- GE Aerospace and Lockheed Martin ran direct-connect tests of a liquid-fueled rotating detonation ramjet at GE Research in Niskayuna (announced Jan 14, 2026). The tests demonstrated ignition and cruise conditions; this was a ground test, not flight. [S], company PR — [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-and-lockheed-martin-demonstrate-rotating-detonation-ramjet-hypersonic); [Lockheed](https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2026-01-14-GE-Aerospace-and-Lockheed-Martin-Demonstrate-Rotating-Detonation-Ramjet-for-Hypersonic-Missiles). GE is also building out Mach 5 wind tunnels [S] — [link](https://www.fanaticalfuturist.com/2025/08/ge-aerospace-builds-out-mach-5-wind-tunnels-to-test-weapons-and-aircraft/)
- Hermeus Quarterhorse Mk 2.1 (an F-16-size uncrewed testbed toward a turbine-based combined cycle) first flew Mar 2, 2026, subsonic. It reached Mach 1.21 on its third flight, May 26, 2026, at White Sands. It is still far from hypersonic. [S] — [AIAA, 27 May 2026](https://aiaa.org/2026/05/27/hermeus-reaches-supersonic-speed-in-historic-quarterhorse-test-flight/); [heise](https://heise.de/-11201503)
- Aerojet Rocketdyne (L3Harris) RDE work: not researched this session (gap).

### Inferences
- US detonation and combined-cycle work is at the same rough technology-readiness stage as China's published work: ground direct-connect tests and small flights. Neither side has shown an operational detonation-powered weapon. Claims of an "exotic propulsion lead" therefore rest on research papers, not deployed capability.
- The binding US constraints are production rate (6-7 of 12 rounds per year), cost (about $41-67M per round) and test cadence, not the physics.

### Gaps
- HACM flight-test status in FY2026 is unknown.
- I did not verify the total FY2027 hypersonics request.
- I did not check the Stratolaunch Talon-A and MACH-TB test-cadence programs (relevant to the test-rate gap).

## Russia (brief comparison)

### Takeaway
Russia was first to field: Avangard in Dec 2019, plus Kinzhal and Zircon. It has used Kinzhal and Zircon in Ukraine, where Kinzhal, a maneuvering air-launched ballistic missile rather than a true HGV, was reported intercepted by Patriot [M]. That record is evidence that "hypersonic" does not by itself mean invulnerable.

### Cited Findings
- Avangard HGV on the SS-19, deployed Dec 2019, "reportedly reaching speeds of Mach 20"; Kinzhal (MiG-31) fired in Ukraine; Zircon first fired into Ukraine Feb 2024. [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)

### Inferences
- Combat use in Ukraine has not shown strategically decisive effects (my inference; Patriot interception of Kinzhal in May 2023 is [M]).

### Gaps
- I did not research Oreshnik (Nov 2024) or Russian scramjet work.

## Expert assessments: is China ahead, and do hypersonics change the strategic balance?

### Takeaway
US officials broadly agree that China leads in fielded hypersonic arsenal, test cadence and ground-test infrastructure. Independent physicists argue that the strategic advantages of boost-glide are overstated: slower than depressed-trajectory ICBMs at intercontinental range, and visible to space sensors. The defensible advantage is theater-level: maneuverability against defenses and short warning for anti-ship and anti-base strikes. That supports "important military competition" more than "most important arms race."

### Cited Findings
- Tracy and Wright (Science & Global Security, 2020) modeled boost-glide missiles. They found these weapons travel intercontinental distances more slowly than comparable depressed-trajectory ballistic missiles and remain visible to existing space-based sensors for most of flight. [S] — [Science & Global Security](https://scienceandglobalsecurity.org/archive/2020/12/modelling_the_performance.html); [UCS blog, Tracy](https://blog.ucs.org/ctracy/setting-the-record-straight-on-hypersonic-weapons); [IEEE Spectrum](https://spectrum.ieee.org/hypersonic-missiles-are-being-hyped)
- Pavel Podvig, quoted by CRS, says hypersonic weapons "don't change much in terms of strategic balance and military capability." CRS also lays out the opposing concern: short flight time and unpredictable paths compress decision time and create ambiguity over targets and warheads. [V] — [CRS R45811](https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2025-08-27_R45811_41dc1d17aff8254c390cc2827f5b7a9c24e3b780.html)
- CRS notes US hypersonic mission requirements "remain undefined" and that cost-effectiveness against alternatives is uncertain. [V] — same
- The comparison often cited for infrastructure: China's Mach 30 JF-22 against Notre Dame's Mach 10 tunnel; "about 12" Chinese hypersonic tunnels, "building about one every six months" (CEO quote). [S] — [NTSA/National Defense, Jul 2024](https://www.ntsa.org/news-and-archives/2024/7/24/testing-top-of-mind-as-us-lags-china-in-hypersonics-race)

### Inferences
- On the tweet's claim: in hypersonics China clearly leads in fielded inventory and test tempo, by roughly 5+ years in fielding (DF-17 around 2019-20 against Dark Eagle in 2025-26). In detonation and combined-cycle "exotic" propulsion, neither side has a fielded system, and China's lead is asserted mainly through journal and press claims.
- The strategic effect is mostly conventional and theater-level (Taiwan, carriers, Guam, and now Hawaii via DF-27), not a transformation of nuclear deterrence. That makes "more important than AI" hard to sustain: AI is a general-purpose enabler across all of these systems. This is my judgment, not a sourced finding.

### Gaps
- I found no recent (2025-26) CSIS or RAND quantitative net assessment of China's lead. Expert views here come from older sources (2020-2024) plus official statements.
- I did not find public test-per-year statistics for either country.
